title: Experts disagree on new ~/.paqad-ai/locks/team-plugin.lock
context:
Chief architect: All three seats agree; this one is the most complete because it adds the clone timeout. It is a pick only because the security-auditor claim is must-level. Spec it as: the lock directory holds the owner pid and start time; a lock whose pid is gone or that is older than 600 seconds is removed and taken over at once; git clone runs with its own timeout below the 590 second wait; a waiter that still times out follows the failed-install path (exit 0, the verbatim notice once per session, no second clone) and the next session retries. That last part is not a new choice: it follows owner decision 1 together with the #616 part 3 rule that a broken install never blocks edits.

Target: new ~/.paqad-ai/locks/team-plugin.lock
- security-auditor: a lock left by a crashed or cancelled first install must be taken over after a set age (for example older than 600 seconds or its owner pid gone); otherwise every later session waits 590 s and then runs with enforcement off forever
- integration-architect: A lock left by a launcher killed mid-clone (session closed, 600 s cancel) blocks every later first install for 590 s and then fails; the lock needs an owner pid and age so a stale lock is taken over, and the clone itself needs a timeout shorter than the SessionStart timeout.
- performance-analyst: a launcher killed mid-clone (the 600-second cancel, a closed laptop) leaves the lock directory behind, and every later session would wait the full 590 seconds; the lock needs an owner pid and age so a stale lock is broken at once
